title: This Bird Hasn't Landed Since Last Summer, and It Won't Until Spring

scenes.text: This bird hasn't landed since last summer.
Scientists at Lund University fitted common swifts with tiny loggers and followed them for ten months.
scenes.keywords: common swift in hand bird tag

scenes.text: Some never touched down once. The rest spent over 99.5 percent of that time in the air.
They eat insects on the wing, drink on the wing, and climb two to three kilometres every dawn and dusk.
Those twilight climbs may be when they nap, gliding slowly back down.
They land only to breed. Over a twenty-year life that adds up to seven round trips to the Moon. Still no landing.
scenes.keywords: common swift nest box migration flock

description:
Common swifts can stay airborne for the whole ten-month non-breeding season. Lund University researchers tracked swifts with tiny data loggers (Hedenström et al., Current Biology, 2016): some individuals never landed at all, and the rest were in the air more than 99.5 percent of the time.
They feed and drink in flight, climb to 2-3 kilometres at dawn and dusk, and land only to breed. Over a 20-year life the distance adds up to about seven round trips to the Moon.
Which animal record would you most like to have?

first_comment: Young swifts may stay in the air for two or three years before they first land to breed. Could you go ten months without sitting down?
